claim: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that lets you monitor the HTTP and HTTPS requests that are forwarded to your protected web application resources.
question: What is AWS WAF, in one sentence?

values.display: a web application firewall
monitor the HTTP and HTTPS requests

evidence.quote: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that lets you monitor the HTTP and HTTPS requests that are forwarded to your protected web application resources.

claim: Based on conditions you specify, such as source IP addresses or query string values, the protected resource responds with the requested content, with an HTTP 403 (Forbidden) status code, or with a custom response.
question: How does a resource protected by AWS WAF respond to a request that a rule blocks?

values.display: an HTTP 403 status code (Forbidden)
or with a custom response

evidence.quote: Based on conditions that you specify, such as the IP addresses that requests originate from or the values of query strings, your protected resource responds to requests either with the requested content, with an HTTP 403 status code (Forbidden), or with a custom response.

claim: You associate a web ACL with one or more web application resources, and the associated resources forward incoming requests to AWS WAF for inspection by the web ACL.
question: How do requests reach AWS WAF for inspection?

values.display: forward incoming requests to AWS WAF
associating it with one or more web application resources

evidence.quote: You do this by defining a web access control list (web ACL) and then associating it with one or more web application resources that you want to protect. The associated resources forward incoming requests to AWS WAF for inspection by the web ACL.

claim: Protection packs are the new console location for web ACLs; they simplify web ACL management in the console but do not change the underlying web ACL functionality, and the standard console and the API still work directly with web ACLs.
question: Is an AWS WAF protection pack a different thing from a web ACL?

values.display: they don't change the underlying web ACL functionality
Protection packs are the new location for web ACLs

evidence.quote: Protection packs are the new location for web ACLs and simplify web ACL management in the console, but they don't change the underlying web ACL functionality. When using the standard console or the API, you'll still work directly with web ACLs.

note: d001. Naming: the exam says web ACL; the new console says protection pack.

claim: A rule is not an AWS WAF resource: it exists only in the context of a web ACL (protection pack) or a rule group, whereas a web ACL and a rule group are AWS WAF resources.
question: Can an AWS WAF rule exist on its own, outside a web ACL or rule group?

values.display: A rule is not an AWS WAF resource.
only exists in the context of

evidence.quote: A rule is not an AWS WAF resource. It only exists in the context of a protection pack (web ACL) or rule group.
A rule group is an AWS WAF resource.

claim: A web ACL (protection pack) and any AWS WAF resources it uses must be in the Region where the associated resource is located; for CloudFront distributions this Region is US East (N. Virginia).
question: In which Region must you create a web ACL for a regional resource, and for a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: must be located in the Region where the associated resource is located
US East (N. Virginia)

evidence.quote: The protection pack (web ACL) and any AWS WAF resources that it uses must be located in the Region where the associated resource is located. For Amazon CloudFront distributions, this is set to US East (N. Virginia).

claim: AWS WAF is available globally for CloudFront distributions, but you must use US East (N. Virginia) to create the web ACL and any resources it uses, such as rule groups, IP sets and regex pattern sets.
question: Where do you create the web ACL, rule groups and IP sets for a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: available globally for CloudFront distributions
you must use the Region US East (N. Virginia)

evidence.quote: AWS WAF is available globally for CloudFront distributions, but you must use the Region US East (N. Virginia) to create your protection pack (web ACL) and any resources used in the protection pack (web ACL), such as rule groups, IP sets, and regex pattern sets.

claim: Choosing the Region option "Global (CloudFront)" in an interface is identical to choosing US East (N. Virginia), us-east-1.
question: What does the Region choice "Global (CloudFront)" mean in AWS WAF?

values.display: identical to choosing Region US East (N. Virginia)
Global (CloudFront)

evidence.quote: Choosing this is identical to choosing Region US East (N. Virginia) or "us-east-1".

claim: When AWS WAF monitors and manages web requests for a protected regional resource, it keeps all data in the same Region as the protected resource.
question: Does AWS WAF move request data out of the Region of a protected regional resource?

values.display: keeps all data in the same Region

evidence.quote: When monitoring and managing web requests for a protected regional resource, AWS WAF keeps all data in the same Region as the protected resource.

claim: You can associate each AWS resource with only one web ACL (protection pack); one web ACL can be associated with many resources (one-to-many).
question: Can one resource, such as an ALB, have two AWS WAF web ACLs at the same time?

values.display: with only one protection pack (web ACL)
one-to-many

evidence.quote: You can associate each AWS resource with only one protection pack (web ACL). The relationship between protection pack (web ACL) and AWS resources is one-to-many.

claim: A web ACL that you have associated with a CloudFront distribution cannot be associated with any other AWS resource type, though it can be associated with more CloudFront distributions.
question: Can the web ACL of a CloudFront distribution also protect an Application Load Balancer?

values.display: with any other AWS resource type
one or more CloudFront distributions

evidence.quote: You can associate a protection pack (web ACL) with one or more CloudFront distributions. You cannot associate a protection pack (web ACL) that you have associated with a CloudFront distribution with any other AWS resource type.

claim: You can associate a web ACL only with an Application Load Balancer within AWS Regions; you cannot associate one with an Application Load Balancer on AWS Outposts.
question: Can AWS WAF protect an Application Load Balancer that runs on AWS Outposts?

values.display: an Application Load Balancer within AWS Regions
an Application Load Balancer that is on AWS Outposts

evidence.quote: You can only associate a protection pack (web ACL) to an Application Load Balancer within AWS Regions. For example, you cannot associate a protection pack (web ACL) to an Application Load Balancer that is on AWS Outposts.

claim: A web ACL that you associate with an AWS Amplify app must be created in the Global (CloudFront) Region; Regional web ACLs are not compatible with Amplify.
question: Which kind of web ACL protects an AWS Amplify app?

values.display: in the Global CloudFront Region
they are not compatible with Amplify

evidence.quote: You must create any protection pack (web ACL) that you want to associate with an Amplify app in the Global CloudFront Region. You might already have a Regional protection pack (web ACL) in your AWS account, but they are not compatible with Amplify.

claim: You cannot associate an Amazon Cognito user pool with a web ACL that uses the Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) or account takeover prevention (ATP) managed rule group.
question: Can a web ACL that uses the ATP or ACFP managed rule group protect a Cognito user pool?

values.display: You can't associate an Amazon Cognito user pool

qualifiers.condition: web ACL uses AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet or AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet

evidence.quote: You can't associate an Amazon Cognito user pool with a protection pack (web ACL) that uses the AWS WAF Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) managed rule group `AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet` or the AWS WAF Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP) managed rule group `AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet`.

claim: Before deploying a web ACL for production traffic, AWS advises testing and tuning it in a staging or test environment, then testing and tuning the rules in count mode with production traffic before enabling them.
question: How does AWS advise rolling out a new web ACL without blocking good users?

values.display: test and tune your rules in count mode
in a staging or testing environment

evidence.quote: Before you deploy your protection pack (web ACL) for production traffic, test and tune it in a staging or testing environment until you are comfortable with the potential impact to your traffic. Then test and tune your rules in count mode with your production traffic before enabling them.

claim: The Count action tracks web traffic without changing how it is handled; you can use it for monitoring and to test new rules before switching them to allow or block matching requests.
question: What is the Count action of AWS WAF used for?

values.display: track your web traffic without modifying how you handle it
to test your new web request handling rules

evidence.quote: You can use the Count action to track your web traffic without modifying how you handle it. You can use this for general monitoring and also to test your new web request handling rules.

claim: With Firewall Manager you set up protections once and the service automatically applies them across your accounts and resources, even as you add new accounts and resources.
question: Does Firewall Manager protect accounts and resources that are added after a policy is created?

values.display: you set up your protections just once
even as you add new accounts and resources

evidence.quote: With Firewall Manager, you set up your protections just once and the service automatically applies them across your accounts and resources, even as you add new accounts and resources.
